findings.title: Sharded queries are interpolated twice
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() at line 52, then later executes each shard group through runSplitQuery(). runSplitQuery() was changed to also map every incoming target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() in querySplitting.ts line 299. As a result, sharded expressions are interpolated again after the __stream_shard__ matcher has been injected. The added test even expects five interpolation calls for one target. Template interpolation is not guaranteed to be idempotent; repeated calls can duplicate ad-hoc filters or reinterpret variable syntax introduced by the first interpolation. Interpolation should be performed in only one layer.

findings.title: Queries that interpolate to empty expressions are not skipped
findings.body: runSplitQuery() filters targets on query.expr before calling applyTemplateVariables(). If a raw expression is a template variable that resolves to an empty string, the target passes the non-empty filter, becomes empty after interpolation, and is still grouped and sent to Loki. This can create invalid empty queries. Add a non-empty expr filter after interpolation; the same problem exists in runShardSplitQuery().

findings.title: Shard splitting keeps targets that become empty after interpolation
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() filters request.targets by the raw query.expr before interpolation. A target whose expression is a variable that expands to an empty string will still enter splitQueriesByStreamShard(), potentially causing shard-label lookups for an empty selector and sending an empty query downstream. Targets should be filtered again after applyTemplateVariables().
